candidates.name: Glasgow Cathedral
candidates.content: This was built in 1197 but much modified in the 13th century and is a fine example of medieval Gothic. It's dedicated to St Mungo, the city's patron saint, who is buried in the crypt. The Church of Scotland doesn't have bishops so

candidates.name: Gallery of Modern Art
candidates.content: It houses rotating exhibitions of contemporary work; there isn't a permanent collection, but exhibitions generally reside for several months. In the basement is one of Glasgow's many public libraries. The building was erected in 1

candidates.name: People's Palace
candidates.content: This is a great folk museum, telling the history of Glasgow and its people from 1750 to 2000. One of Billy Connolly's banana boots is on display. The Winter Gardens are a large adjacent glasshouse. As of May 2026, the museum and g

candidates.name: Willow Tea Rooms
candidates.content: The temperance activist Kate Cranston established a chain of artistic tea rooms, where citizens (especially women) could enjoy non-alcoholic refreshments in genteel surroundings. Her designer was Charles Rennie Mackintosh, and thi

candidates.name: The Museum of Piping
candidates.content: The home of the bagpipes is in the former Cowcaddens Free Church. The museum shows 300 years of piping history, mainly showing Scottish bagpipes, but also showing Northumbrian pipes and some from Poland, Hungary, Italy and Spain.

candidates.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
candidates.content: Magnificent public gallery and museum, opened in 1901 as a legacy of the 1888 International Exhibition. It's in red sandstone, in sort-of Spanish Baroque via St Pancras, and was refurbished in 2006. Extensive collections and displ

candidates.name: Hunterian Art Gallery
candidates.price: Gallery free, Mackintosh House £8 adult, £6 conc, child free
candidates.content: It holds a huge collection of work by Whistler, Rennie Mackintosh, the Scottish Colourists and the Glasgow Boys. The Mackintosh House is a reconstruction of the interior of CRM's nearby home, which was lost to university expansion

candidates.name: Botanic Gardens
candidates.hours: Gardens 7AM to dusk, glasshouses noon to 4PM
candidates.content: Extensive gardens established in 1842 besides the River Kelvin, with tropical and temperate plants. Its distinctive landmark is the Kibble Palace, a 19th-century wrought-iron temperate glasshouse, rebuilt 2004-06.

candidates.name: Glasgow Science Centre
candidates.content: Science museum with hundreds of interactive exhibits for children. You pay extra for the IMAX cinema, planetarium and the 125-metre Glasgow Tower (summer only), the only tower in the world which can rotate 360 degrees from its bas

candidates.name: Riverside Museum
candidates.content: Offers an excellent collection of vehicles and models telling the story of transport by land and sea, with a unique Glasgow flavour. Besides the usual rail locomotives, buses, trams, cars and planes, the museum also includes a rec

candidates.name: House for an Art Lover
candidates.content: In 1901 a German design magazine ran a competition for a Haus eines Kunstfreundes, a house for an art lover. Charles Rennie Macintosh's entry was late and incomplete so it was disqualified, but awarded a special prize for its crea

candidates.name: Queen's Cross Church
candidates.content: The only church built to a design by Rennie Mackintosh, opened in 1899 for what was then the Free Church. They'd split with the Church of Scotland in 1843 but were reconciled in 1929, so the building continued as C of S until it c

candidates.name: Burrell Collection
candidates.content: Sir William Burrell (1861-1958) was a shipping magnate who amassed a huge art collection. He gifted it to the city with the condition that it should be displayed in a nearby yet rural setting, and this was difficult to satisfy unt

candidates.name: St Mungo's Museum of Religious Life and Art
candidates.content: This depicts Glasgow's patron saint and the growth of Christianity in the city, and of other faiths practised locally and worldwide.

candidates.name: Sharmanka Kinetic Theatre
candidates.content: "Sharmanka" is Russian for "barrel-organ" and it's a kinetic gallery. It has dingbat machines created by Eduard Bersudsky, described somewhere between Heath Robinson and Jean Tinguely.

candidates.name: Glasgow Green
candidates.content: is the extensive green space north bank of the Clyde. It was created in 1450 as separate plots of soggy grazing land, which were combined and drained. It became an area for bleaching and drying, mass protests and inflammatory spee

candidates.name: Kelvin Hall
candidates.content: is across the street from Kelvingrove and mirrors its style. This was the city's main event and exhibition venue until SECC opened in 1985, see "Do". It's since been a bit of everything and nowadays is a study and research outpost

candidates.name: Glasgow University
candidates.content: main Gilmorehill campus is a district of half a square mile, bounded to the east by the River Kelvin, to the north by Great Western Road, south by Dumbarton Road, and west by Byres Rd - by Subway use Hillhead. It was founded in 14

candidates.name: Scotland Street School
candidates.content: This school, opened in 1906, was Charles Rennie Mackintosh's last major building. It was a wonderful Art Nouveau design (so naturally it was way over budget) and closed in 1979 when the Gorbals slums were demolished and school enr

candidates.name: Glasgow Vintage Vehicle Trust
candidates.hours: Open to the public on event days only, usually the first Sun of the month spring to autumn, plus an Annual Open Weekend in October. Guided tours by advance booking
candidates.content: A volunteer-run charity caring for a large collection of historic buses, coaches and commercial vehicles in a working bus garage. Many of the vehicles still run, and on open days visitors can board them and take short rides. Check

candidates.name: City Chambers
candidates.content: The City Council headquarters were built in 1888 in Italian Renaissance style. Tours take in the marble staircases, lobbies, debating chamber and banqueting hall. Public tours are conducted M-F at 10:30AM and 2:30PM. Tickets for t

candidates.name: Tenement House
candidates.price: Adult £8.50, conc £6, child £1, NTS / NT free
candidates.content: Miss Agnes Toward was a shorthand typist who lived here 1911-1965 and never changed or discarded a thing. So it's a wonderful gas-lit Edwardian time-warp, now in the keeping of the National Trust for Scotland.

candidates.name: Mitchell Library
candidates.content: Grand Edwardian Baroque pile endowed by the Mitchell tobacco fortune and opened in 1911. It houses a huge municipal public reference library, with over a million volumes and many more primary source archives for tracing family and

candidates.name: Fossil Grove
candidates.content: The remains of an ancient forest of Lepidodendron, extinct giant quillworts. About 330 million years ago this area flooded with mud, which killed the trees but made casts of their trunks. They were discovered during quarrying in 1

candidates.name: Tall Ship
candidates.content: The Glenlee was built in 1896, a three-masted cargo barque. She plied to Australia then was sold for use as a Spanish training vessel. She was eventually laid up in Ferrol, and in 1990 on the verge of being scrapped, but was towed

candidates.name: Holmwood House
candidates.content: Wonderful stylish off-beat villa, built in 1858 by the influential Alexander 'Greek' Thomson. It was originally the home of a paper magnate, and a copy was built for another tycoon in Adelaide in 1885. Holmwood had several owners

candidates.name: Greenbank Garden
candidates.price: Adult £8.50 adult, conc £6, NTS / NT free
candidates.hours: Apr-Jun Sep-Oct: Thu-Mon ; Jul Aug: daily
candidates.content: Garden surrounding an 18th-century mansion, which in 1976 passed to the National Trust for Scotland. It has a large walled garden and parterre, and a brilliant display of daffodils and bluebells in spring. The mansion is an events

candidates.name: Provand's Lordship
candidates.content: Glasgow's oldest remaining house, built in 1471, has been renovated to illustrate city life circa 1700.

candidates.name: Britannia Panopticon
candidates.content: The oldest surviving music hall in the world, this was built in Italianate style in 1857, intended for shops but opening as a free-standing entertainment complex. Big names who boosted their early careers here include Stan Laurel

candidates.name: SEC Armadillo
candidates.content: They've capitulated, and re-named this shiny metal venue what Glaswegians have called it since it opened in 1997. It has a 3000-seater auditorium and is part of the "Scottish Event Campus" alongside the SEC Centre and OVO Hydro. T

candidates.name: Glasgow Royal Concert Hall
candidates.content: Stonking great hall completed in 1990, with a main auditorium seating 2475 and four other spaces of 300+. It's home to the Royal Scottish National Orchestra, who perform throughout Scotland. The same management also runs City Hall

candidates.name: Royal Conservatoire of Scotland
candidates.content: Primarily a teaching college but they also put on public performances of classical and contemporary music, ballet and dance, musical theatre, and contemporary drama.

candidates.name: Hampden Park
candidates.content: Scotland's national stadium has a capacity of 51,866 for football matches and 44,000 for athletics. It hosts other sporting events as well as concerts, and houses the Scottish Football Museum. The Scottish men's and women's soccer

candidates.name: The Cathouse
candidates.content: Rock club founded in 1990.

candidates.name: Barrowland Ballroom
candidates.content: Opened in 1934, but rebuilt in ever-so-Sixties style after a fire, this is a popular live venue with 1900 standing capacity. It's renowned for its sprung dance floor and excellent acoustics.

candidates.name: Tron Theatre
candidates.content: This was built over the derelict Tron Kirk in 1980 - the steeple remains. It's a "producing theatre" like Citizens (below), putting on contemporary works.

candidates.name: Partick Thistle
candidates.price: £22 adults, £16 concessions, £6 U16s, for both home and away fans
candidates.content: "The Jags" play in the Scottish Championship, the second tier. They're named for the Partick district but since 1908 have been at Firhill, an all-seater stadium of capacity 10,100 in Maryhill. Getting a ticket shouldn't be a probl

candidates.name: Queen's Park F.C.
candidates.content: Queen's Park play in the Championship, the second tier. Despite an incredible run without a major trophy since 1893, they are still amongst Scotland's most successful clubs with ten Scottish Cups to their name. Historically they p

candidates.name: Nice'N'Sleazy
candidates.content: A student favourite, Sleazy's is a cross between a bar and a nightclub. Live bands most nights downstairs, and the bar upstairs also has small acts. Over 18s only.

candidates.name: King Tut's Wah Wah Hut
candidates.content: Venue for up-and-coming bands, where Oasis and Glasvegas were discovered.

candidates.name: Theatre Royal
candidates.content: What you see now outside is the modern frontage added in 2014, but the interior is the French Renaissance design adopted after the first major fire in 1879; it was rebuilt thus after the second fire in 1896. The venue opened in 18

candidates.name: Citizens Theatre
candidates.content: Legendary theatre in working-class Gorbals: its predecessor opened in 1878 and the Citizens took over in 1945. This is a "producing theatre", creating its own shows from scratch, so it's contemporary and avant-garde work in a Vict

candidates.name: Òran Mór
candidates.content: Entertainment centre in the former Kelvinside Parish Church, with restaurant, pub, nightclub, theatrical and music and events venues, a fixture of the West End social scene. There are regular lunchtime plays in the "A Play, A Pie

candidates.name: Glasgow Film Theatre
candidates.content: Independent cinema opened in 1939 showing classics, and art and foreign-language movies - the advent of "talkies" made these less accessible to British audiences. It hosts the annual Glasgow Film Festival.

candidates.name: Celtic
candidates.alt: the Bhoys, the Hoops, the Celts
candidates.content: Celtic play soccer in the Premiership, Scotland's top tier, and are Scotland's most successful club. The stadium (capacity 60,400) is two miles east of city centre, between A74 London Rd and A728 Clyde Gateway. See the club websit

candidates.name: Rangers
candidates.content: Rangers also play in the Premiership, where since returning they have finished runners-up to Celtic in all but one season. They play at Ibrox Stadium (capacity 50,800) in Govan and are Scotland's second-most successful club. In 20

candidates.name: Glasgow City FC
candidates.content: Glasgow City FC are a women's team playing in the Scottish Women's Premier League, of which they are reigning champions. They're not affiliated with any men's club and play at Petershill Park (capacity: 1,000, 500 seated) in Sprin

candidates.name: Classic Grand
candidates.content: Alternative music venue in a former tacky "adult" cinema.

candidates.name: Wellpark Brewery
candidates.content: Part of Tennent's - that family have been brewing hereabouts since 1556. This is the largest brewery in Scotland and produces Tennent's Lager, their best-seller. They offer a range of tours.

candidates.name: West Brewery
candidates.content: A restaurant and micro brewery serving German trad food (daily to 9PM) and lager and hefeweizen beers. The tour takes 45 min.

candidates.name: Auchentoshan Distillery
candidates.content: This is one of a handful of distilleries producing lowland single malt whisky. Auchentoshan is triple distilled and very smooth, unpeaty and somewhat sweet, so it's a good "novice" whisky to try. (Scoffers might say "breakfast whi

candidates.name: Drygate
candidates.hours: Tours on Sun, bistro and taproom is open daily 11AM-11PM.
candidates.content: This is a micro-brewery at the west end of the Wellpark site - access via John Knox St. It's a joint venture between C&C (owners of Tennents) and the craft brewer Williams Bros. Pub with views into the brewery and outdoor seating.

candidates.name: Clydeside Distillery
candidates.content: This is in the former dock pumphouse; it's owned by Morrison Glasgow Distillers and produces a lowland-style malt. Production began in 2017 so their first whisky came on sale in 2021.

candidates.name: The Counting House
candidates.content: Formerly a flagship branch of the Bank of Scotland, you drink in the splendour of its Victorian hall, or even snuggle in the vaults. Converted into an open plan bar by JD Wetherspoon chain, it’s popular with tourists and locals al

candidates.name: Horseshoe Bar
candidates.content: Good trad pub with food. Its horseshoe-shaped bar is one of the longest continuous bars in Europe. Rock band Travis used to rehearse upstairs before hitting the big time, and one of their Brit Awards is displayed behind the bar.

candidates.name: Clutha & Victoria Bar
candidates.content: Clutha is the ancient name for the Clyde. The name has also been given to its 19th-century river ferries, a Scottish band, a dance, and this pub by the Gorbals Street bridge. In 2013 a police helicopter crashed into it, killing al

candidates.name: Saracen's Head
candidates.content: Nicknamed the “Sarry Heid” by locals, this old school pub (founded 1755, although in a different building) lies at the gateway to the Barrowlands area and the East End. Like many pubs in the area it becomes an exclusive haunt of C

candidates.name: Solid Rock Cafe
candidates.content: Rock and metal-themed pub.

candidates.name: Waxy O'Connors
candidates.content: Eclectically-decorated Irish venue with six bars, nine rooms and three floors and a maze of stairs.

candidates.name: The Ark
candidates.content: Artfully refurbished in 2022, this is a friendly sports bar with a big beer garden, popular with the two nearby universities.

candidates.name: Corinthian Club
candidates.hours: Thu noon-1AM, Fri Sat noon-3AM, Sun noon-6PM
candidates.content: Gorgeously restored bank and law courts, this is now mainly an events venue, but Teller's Bar & Brasserie serves individuals. Smart casual dress code.

candidates.name: Rufus T. Firefly
candidates.content: Rock and metal music venue, with good affordable pub food.

candidates.name: Ottoman Coffee House
candidates.content: Looks nothing from the outside, but within is rich decor and fine food.

candidates.name: Chillies West End
candidates.content: Slick Indian serving in tapas / thali / short-eats style.

candidates.name: Thai Siam
candidates.content: Good Thai fare, but budget it's not.

candidates.name: Paesano Pizza
candidates.content: This serves Neapolitan wood-fired pizzas in a cavernous industrial chic restaurant. Their other outlets are at 471 Great Western Road G12 8HL and at 1038 Pollokshaws Rd G41 3EB.

candidates.name: Brel
candidates.content: Belgian fare, especially moules in a variety of styles. The place ranges over 3 levels serving Belgian and Scottish beers. Beer garden, and sometimes has live entertainment.

candidates.name: The Merchant
candidates.content: Trad pub serving main dishes.

candidates.name: Romans Pizzeria
candidates.content: Industrial looking, relaxed venue.

candidates.name: BLOC+
candidates.content: Innovative bar with unusual dishes. Separate Vegan/Veggie menu. Live music after 9PM.

candidates.name: China Sea
candidates.content: Sound trad Chinese.

candidates.name: Guido's Coronation Restaurant
candidates.content: A Glasgow institution by the gateway to Barrowlands, good reviews for healthy serving and competitive price.

candidates.name: Panda House
candidates.content: Good south-side choice for Cantonese.

candidates.name: Lucky Cottage
candidates.content: Good reviews for this Chinese takeaway, they also do home deliveries.

candidates.name: Barras Market
candidates.content: "Oh ra Barras, oh ra Barras, ye can keep yer Rome or Paris . . . " goes the song. This market occupies the East End blocks between Gallowgate and London Road at the edge of Glasgow Green. It's an essential tourist experience, but
